idiom_name: plain component objects in an array; mixins/Object.assign for the static case
implementation_notes: In JavaScript the object is already a bag of properties, so a component is just an object or class instance and an entity is an array (or a Map keyed by component type) that the update loop walks - the classic container-plus-slots structure collapses into ordinary object composition, and MDN documents mixins and 'prefer composition over inheritance' as the way to combine behaviour from several sources without the single-inheritance limit. Prefer explicit named fields for a fixed capability set and a components collection only when capabilities really change at runtime; when entity counts are large, data-oriented ECS libraries (bitECS) store components in typed arrays indexed by numeric entity ids instead of objects.
pitfalls: Optional calls hide wiring mistakes: c.update?.(...) or entity.physics?.x no-ops silently, so a missing component shows up as behaviour that simply never happens.
Mutating this.components while iterating it skips or repeats components; collect changes and apply them after the pass.
Components written as arrow-function mixins capture this lexically and cannot be reused across entities - use plain methods or pass the entity explicitly.
